# OpenAI's AI-generated math release (Oct 2026), explained from zero

A sourced learning deck, in parallel Chinese and English editions, for readers with only linear algebra, calculus and high-school math. It explains what OpenAI's [`openai/math`](https://github.com/openai/math) release actually claims and how much has been verified.

**What was released:** on 2026-10-06, OpenAI published 722 manuscripts in 372 result families, generated by an unreleased internal model. On 2026-10-07 it withdrew 3 manuscripts over a sign error, leaving 719.

**What the deck covers:** 10 headline results:

- the quasi-Riemann hypothesis
- the irrationality exponent of π
- the matrix multiplication bound ω ≤ 9/4
- the Unique Games Conjecture
- L = RL = BPL
- the chromatic number of the plane being at least 6
- non-amenability of Thompson's group F
- Navier–Stokes blowup with forcing
- relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell
- the Mézard–Parisi formula

It also covers the withdrawn Hodge-related papers as a case study of what goes wrong without formal verification.

**Part II (§17–§22): looking ahead.** Added 2026-10-08. It extrapolates three trend curves:

- METR task-length horizon, doubling about every 129 days.
- Single-attempt solve rate on open problems, anchored at 3% on FrontierMath Erdős.
- Formal-proof cost, about $0.023/line for the Fermat formalization.

Each curve has optimistic, central and pessimistic scenarios. Part II then argues that the bottleneck moves from proofs to statements and specs. It covers what this means for AI-safety debate, singular learning theory, Guaranteed Safe AI and neurosymbolic systems, and ends with a T0–T4 timeline (2026 Q4 → 2030). Every node lists signals that would falsify it. Claims are tagged [data] / [model] / [judgment].

**How each result is presented:** every result gets the same "ladder":

1. A toy example you can compute by hand
2. The real statement
3. Why it was stuck, and for how long
4. What OpenAI claims, quoting the manuscript
5. Verification status: the Lean statement is read line by line, and public expert reactions are collected
6. What it would mean for mathematics, AI and AI safety if it holds

## Read

- **[`notes_en.pdf`](notes_en.pdf)** / **[`notes_en.html`](notes_en.html)**: English edition (start here).
- **[`notes.pdf`](notes.pdf)** / **[`notes.html`](notes.html)**: Chinese edition.

The two editions are maintained in parallel (not machine-translated), so content changes should be made in both build scripts.

**Part III (§23–§32), both editions:** the 从零精讲 / from-zero explainers, one long chapter per headline result. Each chapter builds the result up from basic concepts, with hand-checkable examples and 【检查】/[Check] exercises, and runs to about ten times the length of its Part I section. The Chinese chapters are in [`精讲/`](精讲/) and the English ones in [`精讲/en/`](精讲/en/), both as Markdown. The build scripts render them into the deck with `md2html.py`.

## What "verified" means here

The deck separates three things:

- **Claimed:** stated by OpenAI in the manuscripts.
- **Machine-checked:** a Lean proof exists. Our static audit of the Lean library (122k files, ~26M lines) found 0 `sorry`, 0 added axioms and 0 `native_decide`. Comparator configs allow only the three standard axioms.
- **Faithful:** the Lean statement actually says what the paper claims. This still needs a human to read it, and the deck does that for each headline result.

As of 2026-10-08, no human domain expert had publicly confirmed reading and checking any headline result. Unformalized results (~58%) have no machine check at all. The 3 withdrawn papers were all among them.

The audit was source-level only. We grepped the source and counted Comparator configs, but did not compile the library or run Comparator. Two independent re-checks are linked in the deck: the ζ 7/8 result was compiled under two kernels, and the statement of the 9/4 matrix-multiplication result was reviewed.

Tags used throughout:

- `[P]`: a primary source was read (paper, repo file or Lean source).
- `[R]`: secondary reporting.
- `⚠`: unverified or conflicting.

## Rebuild

```bash
python3 build_notes.py        # → notes.html    (Chinese; chart data computed in figs.py; Part III rendered from 精讲/*.md)
python3 build_notes_en.py     # → notes_en.html (English; figures from figs_en.py; Part III rendered from 精讲/en/*.md)
for f in notes notes_en; do
  "/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome" --headless=new --no-pdf-header-footer \
    --print-to-pdf="$PWD/$f.pdf" "file://$PWD/$f.html"
done
```

## Files

```
openai_math_explained/
├── build_notes.py     ← Chinese deck content (all text)
├── build_notes_en.py  ← English deck content (maintained in parallel)
├── figs.py / figs_en.py ← inline SVG figures (zh / en labels); plotted numbers computed here
├── 精讲/NN_*.md      ← Part III 从零精讲 chapters (Chinese), one per result
├── 精讲/en/NN_*.md   ← the same chapters in English
├── 精讲/scripts/      ← scripts behind every "脚本实算" number in the chapters (see its README)
├── md2html.py         ← minimal dependency-free Markdown → HTML used for Part III
├── _notes_base.css    ← shared visual style (same as cyber_ai_fundamentals / compute_pause_verification)
├── notes.html / notes.pdf         ← Chinese edition
├── notes_en.html / notes_en.pdf   ← English edition
└── README.md
```
